extracted.intended_audience: ship captains, pilots, and crews engaged in long exploratory voyages (early-modern navigation)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance for navigation, shipboard discipline, landing procedures, trading, and dealing with natives during long exploratory sea voyages. Covers signs of land, anchoring, foraging, rationing, security, and leadership measures to avoid mutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sea debris as sign of land
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sea appears greasy, with leaves of trees, grass, herbs, wood, branches, palm nuts, and other things which the waves carry from the shores, and rivers send down when in flood, it is a sign of land being near in the direction of the present course of the wind, or the currents have brought them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such debris is observed the circumstances will indicate what is best to do; generally the land will be towards the quarter whence the wind comes. Exercise care and consider sounding and changing course as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sea life and currents indicate proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are currents... strong, or there are shoals of small fishes which seem to swarm over the sea, or patches of camarones, sea snakes, seals, turtles, much bad water, or some land birds, take care, for the ship will be very near the land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat heavy currents, concentrated sea life, and unusual surface phenomena as warnings to be vigilant for nearby land or shoals; reduce speed, take soundings, and prepare for navigation hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret bird behaviour to judge distance to land
rubrics_metrics.description: Note the direction in which birds fly and whence they come in the morning; if they assemble early and return late, they are far from land; if they assemble late and return early, the land is near.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also note whether birds assemble (nearer land) or are only heard at night and still seen at dawn (very near or sleeping on sea). Use birds' flight direction and timing to estimate bearing to land.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species-specific bird indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: If the birds met with are piqueros, ducks, widgeons, gulls, estopegados, terns, sparrowhawks, flamingos or siloricos, it is a sign that the land is very near; but if there are only boobies... so much care is not necessary, because these birds are found far from land, and the same may be said of boatswain birds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use knowledge of species' typical range: some birds (boobies, boatswain birds) can be far from land and are less reliable indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Birds flying together or wounded-flight as proximity sign
rubrics_metrics.description: If all the birds, or part of them, fly together, it is a sign of proximity to land; note whether some fly as if wounded, seeking land on one side or the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrated flight or birds appearing to seek land should prompt increased caution and search for anchorage or shoals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sea colour patches indicate bottom type
rubrics_metrics.description: If patches of brown water are seen on the sea, it is a sign that there are rocks near the surface; if the patches are white, it is a sign of a sandy bottom, with little depth; a black patch is a sign of ooze and mud; and a green patch points to a bottom covered with weeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any sea colour different from the ordinary deep dark blue requires care and usually soundings; act accordingly to avoid grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unusual night sea sounds require special vigilance
rubrics_metrics.description: If at night the sea should be heard to make sounds greater than is usual... it is necessary to exercise care, and much more... All the above signs cause an obligation to be very careful and to get soundings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine auditory signs with visual/surface indicators and take immediate soundings, reduce sail, and post extra lookouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put confidence in God but practise seamanship
rubrics_metrics.description: While all these signs point to land or to rocks... it is only in God that we must put our confidence, for it is He alone who knows, and who can guide and save the people and the ship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faith is counselled as moral support, but it is paired with the practical injunction to exercise all necessary navigational vigilance and precautions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep strict night and day lookout in port
rubrics_metrics.description: After anchoring in any port, a careful look-out should be kept both by day and night, for the natives are great swimmers and divers, and might wedge up the rudder, cut the hawsers, or set fire to the ship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In suspicious places have a guard in the boat at night over the buoys or visit buoys many times; never relax watches while anchored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit number of natives aboard
rubrics_metrics.description: Take care not to allow so many natives on board the ship as would be able to overpower the crew; and even when they are few, great evil may come to them as well as to us, from ignorance of our arms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep numbers controlled; treat small groups with caution; avoid situations where natives could seize control or provoke conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land only by day and choose clear landing-places
rubrics_metrics.description: In effecting a landing, it should always be by day, and never at night. The landing-place should be level and clear of woods, or at least as well situated in these respects as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer open, level beaches; avoid wooded, concealed approaches; plan landings with daylight for reconnaissance and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dogs and arms when landing; march in order
rubrics_metrics.description: Send dogs in front to discover ambushes, with arms ready, marching together and in order, and entering passes with caution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive security on shore parties: scouts (dogs), well-armed detachments, organized formation, and slow, cautious advance into unfamiliar terrain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natives concealment tactics to anticipate
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep in mind that the natives usually get behind rocks or trees, or stretch themselves flat on the ground even in level places, concealed only by the grass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect concealment, pits, and ambushes; clear lines of sight and probe suspected areas before sending full parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detain chiefs as hostages but treat them well
rubrics_metrics.description: If possible, chiefs or other natives who appear to be of consequence should be kept in the ship as hostages, but well treated and given presents of things that they seem to like most.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use high-status captives as guarantees and for diplomacy; provide respectful treatment and gifts to maintain goodwill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct barter through a single representative and project value
rubrics_metrics.description: The barter should be conducted by one of us, who should always give the natives to understand that the things are of great value, as they really are for them; and this because they do not value their own things much, and ours but little.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralize trade negotiations with a chosen person to avoid confusion; use presentation and manners to signal value and avoid exploitation that provokes resentment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gather intelligence from natives and record names
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn from the natives whether there are other islands or extensive lands near, if they are inhabited, of what colour are the natives, whether they eat human flesh, if they are friendly or carry on war. Enquire whether they have gold... If they have names for them, write the names down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use signs and gifts to obtain geographic, cultural, and resource information; document local toponyms and commodity names for future reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not underestimate natives; expect pilfering
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not think little of the natives, for they are pilferers and runners, and when they come for that, they know well how to do it;... which is what ought to be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate petty theft and opportunistic behavior; maintain disciplined watch and storage of valuables to prevent loss and escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not blindly follow natives' guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not follow the guidance of the natives except with great caution. Never trust or believe in them on any occasion whether they show much or little sign of friendship, because their custom is to watch on the roads and to make pits covered with earth and grass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat local guides with skepticism; verify routes and have secure escorts; expect deception used to lure parties into traps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent mingling of crew and natives
rubrics_metrics.description: Never allow our people to mix with the natives, nor leave them to join company, owing to the danger that, on a given signal, three or four may fall upon and carry off one of ours to meet the fate which they may want to inflict on him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce separation between crew and locals; prohibit unsupervised fraternization to avoid ambushes or abductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold interviews in cleared space with distance and guard the back
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasions when it is desirable to have an interview with the natives, it should always be in a cleared space, with a good distance between the two parties, and the Chief... standing in the space, so as to concert with him what they desire or ask for. It is always necessary to see that the back is safe without ceasing to watch or even turning the face, but always the whole body. And, when obliged, let it be back to back, with the shields in front.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange meetings so that both sides are visible and protected; maintain tactical positioning (back-to-back, shields) to cover all approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retreat embarkation guard procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If it should be necessary to embark in retreat, either in presence or absence of the enemy, half the arquebusiers and shield-bearers should face the natives, that the other half may embark safely; and those embarked are quickly to turn, making the same guard as the one made by those on shore until all are embarked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use phased embarkation with overlapping covering fire and shields to ensure safe withdrawal under threat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not eat unknown food; watch for poison
rubrics_metrics.description: Take care not to feed on the things which the natives present to be eaten, because they know how to play tricks. ... Care should be taken to look out for poison put into the water or food. Vegetables and fruits should not be eaten unless known before, or unless they have been seen to be used as food by birds and monkeys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain armed readiness when receiving food; test unfamiliar items only after observation of animals using them or other verification; keep personal weapons and avoid hands-free receptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not mistreat or destroy natives' property
rubrics_metrics.description: In ports where natives come to give assistance, never ill-use them nor detain them... nor cut down their fruit trees, nor injure their crops, nor destroy their houses or canoes; for all such acts cost them very dear... For this cause they seek for vengeance, and withdraw food supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid punitive or destructive actions that provoke long-term hostility and loss of cooperation; use restraint and diplomacy; threaten capability if necessary but refrain from actual destruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: When following natives' reports, bring the informants
rubrics_metrics.description: For two reasons the natives may give false information... When it is decided to follow up any of their notices by sea or land, the same natives that have given the information should be made to accompany the party, to secure this point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require the original informants to guide and be accountable when pursuing leads; this reduces deception and improves local knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use arquebus fire and suited steps to disperse attackers
rubrics_metrics.description: In forced attacks, arquebus fire should be in the air, with or without ball; and by taking other steps suited to the occasion, they will be made to fly or desist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer warning/dispersal shots rather than immediate killing; adapt tactics to situation to minimize casualties and secure retreat or deterrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forage with well-armed escort and assess opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: When seeking for wood, water, or provisions, a boat should be sent with well-armed men to over-awe the natives, even in places where it does not seem likely that there will be a rupture with them. If they begin to offer opposition, and the necessity is not very great, it will be as well to return to the ship, and await a better opportunity. If the necessity is great, send a large number of guards to protect the foraging party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess necessity before escalating; prefer deterrence and withdrawal over unnecessary combat; scale security proportionally to need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act as fathers but watch as enemies; preserve right intentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the danger of offending the natives, or being offended by them. The position should be as fathers to children, but they must be watched as if they were known enemies. Our part is always to be in the right, with open and honest intentions; then God will help us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a posture of benevolent authority combined with constant vigilance; maintain moral high ground while protecting crew and assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care for the sick and dead: confession, wills, and inventories
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person should fall sick, he should presently confess and make his will. If he should die, it is ordered that the master, with a clerk, should make an inventory of his goods, and take charge of them, in order to carry out the wishes of the deceased. If he dies intestate, the same care is to be taken in making an inventory, and in taking care of the goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper religious, legal, and administrative procedures for illness and death onboard to settle affairs and preserve discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making under time pressure: consult and record
rubrics_metrics.description: All these things are to be complied with, without exceeding them, unless time is very pressing. In that case, if it appears necessary, counsel should be taken with the Master and Pilot, officers, and other important persons, and with the opinions of all of them, signed with their names, what is agreed upon may be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When deviating from standing orders due to urgent circumstances, obtain written collective counsel from senior officers to legitimize actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Water rationing and overseen distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The Captain... deemed it necessary to reduce the allowance of water. Twelve or fifteen jars of water that were consumed each day he reduced to three or four jars. He was present when it was served out, saw the hatchway closed, and kept the keys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce strict rationing when supplies are low; supervise distribution personally and control access to reserves to prevent hoarding and waste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovate to produce fresh water (distillation)
rubrics_metrics.description: He ordered a brick oven to be built... in order to make sweet water from sea water, with a copper instrument he had with him, by means of distillation. They got two or three jars full every day... this invention... promises... to turn out in fifteen hours eight, nine, and ten jars of fresh water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use shipboard ingenuity to distil seawater; prioritize technologies and methods that conserve fuel and increase daily yield to sustain the crew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain formation and require pilots' observational reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The Captain put out a flag on the topmast for the ships to close and the pilots to report in what latitude they were, how many leagues from Lima, the observations the ships had taken respecting lee-way, winds, and the variation of the needle, also the bearing of the islands...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require coordinated reporting of position, leeway, winds, compass variation and bearings; use signals to summon pilots and consolidate navigation data for command decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership vigilance against mutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: A mutiny can only begin between two or three... To corrupt the rest there must be sounding of people, friendships, and much intercourse... He considered that patience and vigilance were two very necessary things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for early signs: favoritism, waste of provisions among friends, excessive private consultations, quarrels with officers; address suspicions directly, reinforce mission purpose, and speak publicly to restore morale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspire crew by asserting mission purpose and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Captain said to the whole crew that the Royal Majesty despatched those ships at great expense, to see whether there was in this unknown part of the earth the land which was supposed to exist... all might be quite sure that they would have to search for it... even if it cost all their lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use speeches to remind crew of higher purpose and obligations; rebuke shirking and emphasize honour and duty to sustain resolve during hardship.
